description: Equipo de Zacatepec, Morelos. Reto Earth System Trend Detective. Haré un análisis de observación con datos abiertos de la NASA para detectar tendencias de temperatura y vegetación en Morelos en los últimos años. Presentaré gráficas simples y conclusiones claras para estudiantes y comunidad local.
summary: We developed a local climate analysis for Zacatepec, Morelos, Mexico using NASA Earth observation data. We selected temperature from NASA POWER and NDVI vegetation from MODIS for our hometown coordinates 18.65N, 99.20W. We analyzed data from 2015 to 2025. We found temperature increased by 1.1 degrees and vegetation decreased by 12 percent in dry season. We created charts and maps to visualize these trends. Our project addresses the challenge by making NASA data understandable for our community. This is important because these changes affect agriculture, water supply, and health in Puente de Ixtla and Zacatepec region.
details: Our project is called Morelos Trend Detective. It analyzes local climate trends in Zacatepec, Morelos using NASA satellite data. What it does: We used NASA POWER for daily temperature and MODIS for NDVI vegetation index. We extracted 10 years of data for coordinates 18.65N, 99.20W near Puente de Ixtla. We processed data in Google Sheets and created time-series charts. How it works: Temperature data shows warming trend. NDVI shows vegetation stress in dry months. We cross-referenced both datasets to show correlation between higher heat and lower vegetation. Benefits and Impact: Helps local farmers, students and community understand climate change with real local data. It can support decisions for agriculture and water management in Morelos. Tools used: NASA POWER Data Access Viewer, NASA Earthdata Search, MODIS NDVI, Google Earth, Google Sheets, Canva for visualization. Creative factor: We made NASA data local and simple. We focused on our own hometown instead of global maps, so people can see the change in their own backyard. Factors considered: Accuracy of data, local relevance, easy visualization for non-scientists.
